commit.message:
feat(kanban): batch set-model selectors + time-boxed lane-model override (#829)

* feat(model-policy): require flagship firepower reasons

Guard kanban and delegate_task flagship overrides, persist audit comments atomically, and announce effective spawn routes.\n\nVerified: 55 focused/adjacent pytest cases pass; ruff check and git diff --check pass.

* test(delegate): update strict schema contract

The model/provider/firepower_reason fields are now intentionally advertised.\n\nVerified: 11 tests pass; ruff check and git diff --check pass.

* feat(kanban): batch set-model selectors + time-boxed lane-model override

Routing a batch of workers onto a different provider had exactly two honest
options: N invocations of `set-model`, or editing a profile's config.yaml.
The config edit is the wrong layer — it changes the standing default for every
future spawn, has no expiry, trips fleet-config-lint, and needs a human to
remember to revert it.

BATCH: `set-model` now takes N ids, `--where status=running,ready assignee=x`,
and `--all-active` (terminal rows excluded). One `t_xxx: route=provider/model
applies=next-dispatch` line per card. Validation is atomic across the batch —
an unknown provider or an ungated flagship id refuses everything before any
write, so a partial application can't leave the operator guessing which cards
moved. `--reclaim` releases claims on selected RUNNING cards so they respawn on
the new route now; without it a live worker keeps its old model until it exits.
A single explicitly-named card keeps the original human sentences.

LANE: `lane-model set <provider>/<model> --ttl 2h --reason "…" [--assignee p]`
writes a board-level row applied at spawn to cards with no override of their
own; `show`/`clear` inspect and end it. --ttl is required. Precedence is
per-card > lane > profile default: a card pinned explicitly is never silently
re-routed. Expiry is enforced on the dispatcher clock and the rows are DELETED,
so `lane-model expired (<lane>) -> profile default` is logged exactly once.
Every spawn logs source=card-override|lane-override(<n>s remaining)|
profile-default, and `kanban stats` lists active overrides with remaining TTL.
Applied to the review lane as well as ready — a window that re-routes workers
but strands reviewers on a capped provider blocks everything downstream.

The flagship/firepower predicate is imported from hermes_cli.model_policy
(t_343f0279), not reimplemented. hermes_cli/model_override.py belongs to
t_55547259 and is deliberately NOT forked here.

Verified:
- 24 focused tests green (batch selectors, precedence, TTL boundary, expiry
  reported once, reclaim scope, firepower + provider gates).
- 8/8 mutations killed. Two initially survived and both were real: the TTL
  read-path filter had no test (added one asserting a lapsed row is invisible
  while still in the table), and a CLI-level `task.status == "running"` check
  turned out to be a redundant second copy of reclaim_task's own guard — it was
  removed rather than tested, so the guard has one owner.
- tests/hermes_cli: 8572 passed, 2 failed — both pre-existing on base
  (test_user_providers_model_switch, confirmed by stashing this change).
- 115 passed across the dashboard plugin, dispatcher standby, worker runs and
  kanban tools; 18 passed on the plugin model-override suite.
- End-to-end on an isolated scratch board: batch by ids, batch by --where,
  provider typo refused, flagship refused, lane set/show/clear, stats surfacing,
  and --ttl required.

Schema: lane_model_overrides is created by SCHEMA_SQL, which connect() runs
per path, so existing boards migrate on first open with no separate step.

* fix(kanban): apply lane route before admission and validate batch overrides

Verified 44 focused tests including reviewer regressions, capped-profile lane admission, JSON override and legacy effort paths.

* test(kanban): exercise gateway tick logs and reverse capacity gate

Verified 50 focused tests including gateway idle expiry and both admission directions.

* test(kanban): fail closed before initializing scratch board

Verified 9 scratch-board review regressions; sandbox path checked before DB init.

* fix(kanban): keep card route on JSON effort-only update

Verified 47 focused tests including unified JSON effort-only round trip.

* fix(kanban): gate canonical flagship aliases before routing

Synced model_policy.py verbatim from owning #812 head 207a20d. Reproduced six alias bypasses before the fix; 71 focused tests passed after. Broad Kanban suite: 884 passed, 5 failed (same five inherited on merge-base per Argus round 2), 3 skipped.

* fix(kanban): make set-model batches all-or-nothing under concurrent mutation

`hermes kanban set-model` selected N cards and then wrote them through the
individually-committing `set_model_override` / `set_reasoning_effort`. A card
that changed state AFTER selection (another connection archives it, a worker
claims it) failed midway and left the cards ahead of it pinned: a silently
split route across what the operator issued as ONE action, with no receipt
naming which cards moved. Static prevalidation cannot close this — the defect
lives entirely in the interval between "we checked" and "we wrote".

kanban_db: split the two setters into `_validate_*` (no DB) and `*_locked`
(must already be in a txn) halves, and add `apply_batch_route_writes()`, which
validates every card's arguments up front and then does all the status checks
and all the writes inside ONE `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The per-card status re-read
now runs against the snapshot its UPDATE commits against, so any refusal
unwinds the whole batch. Observers fire only after that commit, so a
rolled-back batch never announces a mutation that did not happen.

Class sweep over every batch mutation shape:
- `lane-model clear --all` had the same defect (list, then loop of separately
  committed deletes, reporting the PRE-loop list). Added
  `clear_all_lane_model_overrides()` — reads and deletes under one txn and
  returns only the rows it actually deleted.
- `--reclaim` cannot be made atomic: it SIGTERMs a live worker, which a
  rollback could not undo. It stays after the route txn, but a failure there
  is no longer silent — each is reported as `t_x: route applied but reclaim
  failed: <why>` with exit 1, alongside the route receipt. Truthful partial
  outcome rather than a hidden one.
- Dismissed with reason: single-target sites (`lane-model set`, `_cmd_reclaim`,
  `reassign_task`, dashboard single PATCH) have no multi-target interval.
  Dashboard `POST /tasks/bulk` is documented independent iteration that already
  returns a complete per-id applied/refused receipt, and mixes irreversible
  transitions an all-or-nothing txn could not undo.

Verified (HERMES_KANBAN_SANDBOX=1, temp HOME, no live board):
- New tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_batch_atomicity.py, 9 tests. The injection
  seam is `_select_batch_tasks` because it exists on both heads, so the file
  runs unmodified against the pre-fix tree.
- RED at prior head d71a16148: 6 failed, 2 passed. Reproduces the reported
  shape exactly — `assert _route(first) == ('ready', None, None, None)` ->
  `At index 1 diff: 'batch-provider' != None`. The 2 passing there are the
  controls (uninterrupted batch, bystander archive), so they discriminate.
- GREEN here: 9/9. Focused set 77 passed; 28 passed after the reclaim-receipt
  and lane-clear-all additions.
- Broad tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban*.py: 894 passed, 5 failed, 3 skipped —
  the same five Argus independently confirmed inherited on clean merge-base
  fdedf3fc2 in round 2.

* fix(kanban): retain receipts after reclaim side effects

Verified: 24 focused atomicity/reassign tests pass; 10 fail on prior head. Dashboard reassign pair RED on prior head, GREEN now (67 dashboard+atomicity tests). Product routes 107 pass; ruff clean. Broad -k kanban: 1406 passed, 32 failed (prior/base inherited subset), 18 skipped. No live board or gateway touched.

* fix(kanban): retain reassign receipt across assign failures

Verified two-connection SQLite lock and new-claim races through CLI/dashboard; 114 focused tests passed and ruff clean.

* fix(kanban): refuse unvalidated provider routes when discovery is empty

Verified 10 fail-before provider-discovery cases and 76 focused tests passing; ruff clean.

* fix(kanban): gate effective lane route at dispatch; recheck batch selector and lane rows under the writer lock

Argus round-7 findings on #829 (t_f08b7589), all reproduced on eaed38366:

1. Dispatch flagship gate checked only the card pin. It now checks the
   route the spawn will use: card pin, else the active lane override,
   against the policy loaded this tick, on ready and review paths. A lane
   route is authorized by the lane's --allow-flagship/--firepower reason or
   the card's "flagship override:" comment. Profile defaults unchanged.
2. apply_batch_route_writes re-evaluates each card's selection predicate
   (status set, assignee set) inside its BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Selector-chosen
   cards that left the set are skipped and named in the receipt; an
   explicitly named card that left the set aborts the batch (nothing
   written). --reclaim acts only on written cards.
3. expire_lane_model_overrides reads and deletes under one writer lock; the
   tick records what still routes each expired lane (board-wide lane,
   renewed window, or profile default) and the gateway/CLI logs name it.
4. clear_lane_model_override reads and deletes under one writer lock; the
   clear receipt reports the row actually deleted and what now routes the
   lane.

Verified: 15 new two-connection regressions (12 RED on eaed38366, 3
controls green on both); 198 focused tests pass; the five Argus probes
no longer reproduce; ruff clean.

---------

Co-authored-by: Kyzcreig <9063726+Kyzcreig@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Apollo <apollo@angventures.io>
Co-authored-by: daedalus-opus <daedalus-opus@angventures.io>

commit.message:
fix(gateway): spool adapter-parked follow-ups before teardown clears them (t_e253d9d5 r4, stacked on #937) (#945)

* fix(gateway): spool adapter-parked follow-ups before teardown clears them

Argus r3 (t_e253d9d5): stop() ran _bounded_adapter_teardown() first;
BasePlatformAdapter.cancel_background_tasks() drains _pending_messages
into the #72680 flush file (no session_id, not replayable as a turn)
and clears the debounce store, so the later restart-spool sweep saw an
empty slot. Real stop -> fresh boot delivered 0/1.

The runner now installs _spool_one_adapter_pending as the adapter's
_shutdown_pending_sink; cancel_background_tasks() calls it after the
late-arrival drain rounds and before the flush/clear. Debounce bursts
are folded into the slot (or spooled directly) first. Entries leave
the slot only once durably spooled; failures still reach the flush.

Verified: new real stop(restart=True) -> fresh start() tests (pending
slot + debounce buffer) 2 passed; RED (2 failed) with the sink not
installed and with the sink never called. Argus r3 probes: real stop
spool 1, boot receipts 1/1. Regression: 16 restart/drain/flush files
186 passed, 2 skipped.

* fix(gateway): restart spool keeps overflow tails and the parked event's identity (t_e253d9d5 r6)

- _spool_adapter_pending_for_restart: _queued_events is a SessionFieldView
  (MutableMapping, not dict); the dict-only gate skipped every /queue
  overflow tail, so '(2 queued)' replayed only the head.
- Spool record v2 carries every MessageEvent dataclass field except
  text/source (top-level), raw_message and the open-interaction echo
  fields; the boot loader rebuilds the same event. A field that cannot be
  stored durably is refused and logged restart_followup_lost field=<name>.
- The post-turn draining site now spools the event itself, not the
  derived transcript/placeholder string.

Tests: real stop(restart=True) -> fresh start() for head+tail order and
per-field identity (slot and overflow carriers, plugin /new stays
non-command), plus the refusal path.

* fix(gateway): post-turn voice transcript still wins in the v2 restart spool (t_e253d9d5 r7)

The v2 spool carries the parked event; the post-turn draining site may
already have transcribed a voice follow-up. Keep that transcript as the
record text and drop the transcribed audio from the carried media so the
replay does not run STT twice; every other event field is still carried.
A media placeholder is not an override (the carried media rebuilds it).

Tests: test_restart_interrupt_intent_followups 20/20 (existing transcript
test was RED on 4db0db5518); 4/4 mutants killed.

---------

Co-authored-by: Kyzcreig <9063726+Kyzcreig@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
feat(kanban): hermes kanban clone - reference clones against shared fleet mirrors (t_dad1edd7) (#947)

* feat(kanban): `hermes kanban clone` - reference clones against shared fleet mirrors (t_dad1edd7)

Workers clone fleet repos by hand into scratch workspaces (159 clones on
2026-09-23, 39 of hermes-home, each a full object store). The dispatcher
never clones, so dedupe has to live in a helper the worker calls.

`hermes kanban clone <url> [dest] [-b branch]` runs
`git clone --reference-if-able <root>/mirrors/<owner>/<repo>.git <url>`
for ANG-Ventures/* and Kyzcreig/* GitHub URLs. Mirrors are created lazily
(bare, flock-serialised, tmp+rename so a half-built mirror is never
visible) with gc.auto=0 / gc.pruneExpire=never: a pruned mirror corrupts
every dependent clone. Non-fleet URLs clone normally; a mirror failure
degrades to a plain clone with a stderr warning. `clone` dispatches before
kb.init_db() - it has no board state.

KANBAN_GUIDANCE gains one line pointing workers at the helper (7311 chars,
cap 8000).

Verified:
- tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_clone.py 15 passed (real git transport via
  url.insteadOf onto local bare repos; alternates present, count-objects
  size 0, never-prune config written, mirror reused, non-fleet plain,
  mirror failure degrades, CLI dispatch never touches kanban.db)
- with test_kanban_tools, test_kanban_cli, test_prompt_builder in a
  scrubbed env: 145 passed, 1 skipped
- live: clone of ANG-Ventures/hermes-home via the helper -> alternates to
  ~/.hermes/mirrors/ANG-Ventures/hermes-home.git/objects, 4.0K objects in
  the checkout (mirror 164M), fsck --connectivity-only clean
- ruff clean

* fix(kanban clone): precious-objects mirrors, forwarded git-clone options, one deletion choke point (t_dad1edd7 r2)

Addresses Argus QA r1 on #947.

B1 test_workspace_deletion_has_one_choke_point: ensure_mirror no longer
calls shutil.rmtree. The mirror is built at a fixed staging path
(<owner>/.<repo>.git.partial) via init --bare + config + fetch and renamed
into place; a failed build is resumed by the next caller instead of deleted.

B3 never-prune: mirrors now get core.repositoryformatversion=1 +
extensions.preciousObjects=true BEFORE the first fetch, so an explicit
`git gc --prune=now` / `git prune` cannot drop objects dependents borrow.
gc.* keys kept as defence in depth. Tests assert literal config values
(not a loop over MIRROR_CONFIG), a behavioural gc --prune=now test with a
precious=False control arm that must corrupt, and the mirror root pinned
to the fleet root under HERMES_HOME=<root>/profiles/<name>.

B5b the helper forwards -q/-v, -n/--no-checkout, --single-branch,

commit.message:
feat(kanban): batch set-model selectors + time-boxed lane-model override (#829)

* feat(model-policy): require flagship firepower reasons

Guard kanban and delegate_task flagship overrides, persist audit comments atomically, and announce effective spawn routes.\n\nVerified: 55 focused/adjacent pytest cases pass; ruff check and git diff --check pass.

* test(delegate): update strict schema contract

The model/provider/firepower_reason fields are now intentionally advertised.\n\nVerified: 11 tests pass; ruff check and git diff --check pass.

* feat(kanban): batch set-model selectors + time-boxed lane-model override

Routing a batch of workers onto a different provider had exactly two honest
options: N invocations of `set-model`, or editing a profile's config.yaml.
The config edit is the wrong layer — it changes the standing default for every
future spawn, has no expiry, trips fleet-config-lint, and needs a human to
remember to revert it.

BATCH: `set-model` now takes N ids, `--where status=running,ready assignee=x`,
and `--all-active` (terminal rows excluded). One `t_xxx: route=provider/model
applies=next-dispatch` line per card. Validation is atomic across the batch —
an unknown provider or an ungated flagship id refuses everything before any
write, so a partial application can't leave the operator guessing which cards
moved. `--reclaim` releases claims on selected RUNNING cards so they respawn on
the new route now; without it a live worker keeps its old model until it exits.
A single explicitly-named card keeps the original human sentences.

LANE: `lane-model set <provider>/<model> --ttl 2h --reason "…" [--assignee p]`
writes a board-level row applied at spawn to cards with no override of their
own; `show`/`clear` inspect and end it. --ttl is required. Precedence is
per-card > lane > profile default: a card pinned explicitly is never silently
re-routed. Expiry is enforced on the dispatcher clock and the rows are DELETED,
so `lane-model expired (<lane>) -> profile default` is logged exactly once.
Every spawn logs source=card-override|lane-override(<n>s remaining)|
profile-default, and `kanban stats` lists active overrides with remaining TTL.
Applied to the review lane as well as ready — a window that re-routes workers
but strands reviewers on a capped provider blocks everything downstream.

The flagship/firepower predicate is imported from hermes_cli.model_policy
(t_343f0279), not reimplemented. hermes_cli/model_override.py belongs to
t_55547259 and is deliberately NOT forked here.

Verified:
- 24 focused tests green (batch selectors, precedence, TTL boundary, expiry
  reported once, reclaim scope, firepower + provider gates).
- 8/8 mutations killed. Two initially survived and both were real: the TTL
  read-path filter had no test (added one asserting a lapsed row is invisible
  while still in the table), and a CLI-level `task.status == "running"` check
  turned out to be a redundant second copy of reclaim_task's own guard — it was
  removed rather than tested, so the guard has one owner.
- tests/hermes_cli: 8572 passed, 2 failed — both pre-existing on base
  (test_user_providers_model_switch, confirmed by stashing this change).
- 115 passed across the dashboard plugin, dispatcher standby, worker runs and
  kanban tools; 18 passed on the plugin model-override suite.
- End-to-end on an isolated scratch board: batch by ids, batch by --where,
  provider typo refused, flagship refused, lane set/show/clear, stats surfacing,
  and --ttl required.

Schema: lane_model_overrides is created by SCHEMA_SQL, which connect() runs
per path, so existing boards migrate on first open with no separate step.

* fix(kanban): apply lane route before admission and validate batch overrides

Verified 44 focused tests including reviewer regressions, capped-profile lane admission, JSON override and legacy effort paths.

* test(kanban): exercise gateway tick logs and reverse capacity gate

Verified 50 focused tests including gateway idle expiry and both admission directions.

* test(kanban): fail closed before initializing scratch board

Verified 9 scratch-board review regressions; sandbox path checked before DB init.

* fix(kanban): keep card route on JSON effort-only update

Verified 47 focused tests including unified JSON effort-only round trip.

* fix(kanban): gate canonical flagship aliases before routing

Synced model_policy.py verbatim from owning #812 head 207a20d. Reproduced six alias bypasses before the fix; 71 focused tests passed after. Broad Kanban suite: 884 passed, 5 failed (same five inherited on merge-base per Argus round 2), 3 skipped.

* fix(kanban): make set-model batches all-or-nothing under concurrent mutation

`hermes kanban set-model` selected N cards and then wrote them through the
individually-committing `set_model_override` / `set_reasoning_effort`. A card
that changed state AFTER selection (another connection archives it, a worker
claims it) failed midway and left the cards ahead of it pinned: a silently
split route across what the operator issued as ONE action, with no receipt
naming which cards moved. Static prevalidation cannot close this — the defect
lives entirely in the interval between "we checked" and "we wrote".

kanban_db: split the two setters into `_validate_*` (no DB) and `*_locked`
(must already be in a txn) halves, and add `apply_batch_route_writes()`, which
validates every card's arguments up front and then does all the status checks
and all the writes inside ONE `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The per-card status re-read
now runs against the snapshot its UPDATE commits against, so any refusal
unwinds the whole batch. Observers fire only after that commit, so a
rolled-back batch never announces a mutation that did not happen.

Class sweep over every batch mutation shape:
- `lane-model clear --all` had the same defect (list, then loop of separately
  committed deletes, reporting the PRE-loop list). Added
  `clear_all_lane_model_overrides()` — reads and deletes under one txn and
  returns only the rows it actually deleted.
- `--reclaim` cannot be made atomic: it SIGTERMs a live worker, which a
  rollback could not undo. It stays after the route txn, but a failure there
  is no longer silent — each is reported as `t_x: route applied but reclaim
  failed: <why>` with exit 1, alongside the route receipt. Truthful partial
  outcome rather than a hidden one.
- Dismissed with reason: single-target sites (`lane-model set`, `_cmd_reclaim`,
  `reassign_task`, dashboard single PATCH) have no multi-target interval.
  Dashboard `POST /tasks/bulk` is documented independent iteration that already
  returns a complete per-id applied/refused receipt, and mixes irreversible
  transitions an all-or-nothing txn could not undo.

Verified (HERMES_KANBAN_SANDBOX=1, temp HOME, no live board):
- New tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_batch_atomicity.py, 9 tests. The injection
  seam is `_select_batch_tasks` because it exists on both heads, so the file
  runs unmodified against the pre-fix tree.
- RED at prior head d71a16148: 6 failed, 2 passed. Reproduces the reported
  shape exactly — `assert _route(first) == ('ready', None, None, None)` ->
  `At index 1 diff: 'batch-provider' != None`. The 2 passing there are the
  controls (uninterrupted batch, bystander archive), so they discriminate.
- GREEN here: 9/9. Focused set 77 passed; 28 passed after the reclaim-receipt
  and lane-clear-all additions.
- Broad tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban*.py: 894 passed, 5 failed, 3 skipped —
  the same five Argus independently confirmed inherited on clean merge-base
  fdedf3fc2 in round 2.

* fix(kanban): retain receipts after reclaim side effects

Verified: 24 focused atomicity/reassign tests pass; 10 fail on prior head. Dashboard reassign pair RED on prior head, GREEN now (67 dashboard+atomicity tests). Product routes 107 pass; ruff clean. Broad -k kanban: 1406 passed, 32 failed (prior/base inherited subset), 18 skipped. No live board or gateway touched.

* fix(kanban): retain reassign receipt across assign failures

Verified two-connection SQLite lock and new-claim races through CLI/dashboard; 114 focused tests passed and ruff clean.

* fix(kanban): refuse unvalidated provider routes when discovery is empty

Verified 10 fail-before provider-discovery cases and 76 focused tests passing; ruff clean.

* fix(kanban): gate effective lane route at dispatch; recheck batch selector and lane rows under the writer lock

Argus round-7 findings on #829 (t_f08b7589), all reproduced on eaed38366:

1. Dispatch flagship gate checked only the card pin. It now checks the
   route the spawn will use: card pin, else the active lane override,
   against the policy loaded this tick, on ready and review paths. A lane
   route is authorized by the lane's --allow-flagship/--firepower reason or
   the card's "flagship override:" comment. Profile defaults unchanged.
2. apply_batch_route_writes re-evaluates each card's selection predicate
   (status set, assignee set) inside its BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Selector-chosen
   cards that left the set are skipped and named in the receipt; an
   explicitly named card that left the set aborts the batch (nothing
   written). --reclaim acts only on written cards.
3. expire_lane_model_overrides reads and deletes under one writer lock; the
   tick records what still routes each expired lane (board-wide lane,
   renewed window, or profile default) and the gateway/CLI logs name it.
4. clear_lane_model_override reads and deletes under one writer lock; the
   clear receipt reports the row actually deleted and what now routes the
   lane.

Verified: 15 new two-connection regressions (12 RED on eaed38366, 3
controls green on both); 198 focused tests pass; the five Argus probes
no longer reproduce; ruff clean.

---------

Co-authored-by: Kyzcreig <9063726+Kyzcreig@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Apollo <apollo@angventures.io>
Co-authored-by: daedalus-opus <daedalus-opus@angventures.io>

* fix(kanban): make set-model batches all-or-nothing under concurrent mutation

`hermes kanban set-model` selected N cards and then wrote them through the
individually-committing `set_model_override` / `set_reasoning_effort`. A card
that changed state AFTER selection (another connection archives it, a worker
claims it) failed midway and left the cards ahead of it pinned: a silently
split route across what the operator issued as ONE action, with no receipt
naming which cards moved. Static prevalidation cannot close this — the defect
lives entirely in the interval between "we checked" and "we wrote".

kanban_db: split the two setters into `_validate_*` (no DB) and `*_locked`
(must already be in a txn) halves, and add `apply_batch_route_writes()`, which
validates every card's arguments up front and then does all the status checks
and all the writes inside ONE `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The per-card status re-read
now runs against the snapshot its UPDATE commits against, so any refusal
unwinds the whole batch. Observers fire only after that commit, so a
rolled-back batch never announces a mutation that did not happen.

Class sweep over every batch mutation shape:
- `lane-model clear --all` had the same defect (list, then loop of separately
  committed deletes, reporting the PRE-loop list). Added
  `clear_all_lane_model_overrides()` — reads and deletes under one txn and
  returns only the rows it actually deleted.
- `--reclaim` cannot be made atomic: it SIGTERMs a live worker, which a
  rollback could not undo. It stays after the route txn, but a failure there
  is no longer silent — each is reported as `t_x: route applied but reclaim
  failed: <why>` with exit 1, alongside the route receipt. Truthful partial
  outcome rather than a hidden one.
- Dismissed with reason: single-target sites (`lane-model set`, `_cmd_reclaim`,
  `reassign_task`, dashboard single PATCH) have no multi-target interval.
  Dashboard `POST /tasks/bulk` is documented independent iteration that already
  returns a complete per-id applied/refused receipt, and mixes irreversible
  transitions an all-or-nothing txn could not undo.

Argus round-7 findings on #829 (t_f08b7589), all reproduced on eaed38366:

1. Dispatch flagship gate checked only the card pin. It now checks the

   the card's "flagship override:" comment. Profile defaults unchanged.
2. apply_batch_route_writes re-evaluates each card's selection predicate
   (status set, assignee set) inside its BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Selector-chosen
   cards that left the set are skipped and named in the receipt; an
   explicitly named card that left the set aborts the batch (nothing
   written). --reclaim acts only on written cards.
3. expire_lane_model_overrides reads and deletes under one writer lock; the
   tick records what still routes each expired lane (board-wide lane,
   renewed window, or profile default) and the gateway/CLI logs name it.
4. clear_lane_model_override reads and deletes under one writer lock; the
   clear receipt reports the row actually deleted and what now routes the
   lane.
